# My plan for this year

Alright, let me think through this. I'm 65 now, been working this land for 40 years. My wife helps me but she's got her own troubles with her back. Two of my sons work in Handan city, one daughter married out. They come back to help during the busy weeks — wheat harvest into maize planting is the worst, only about a week to turn the field around. I can't do that alone anymore.

I have 10.1 mu altogether. Most years I put **7 mu in wheat-maize** like most people around here, and keep **3.1 mu in cotton** on that sandier piece near the road. I know people say cotton isn't worth it anymore, but I've grown it for decades and the family comes back to pick in October. It's a habit, honestly, and the land there isn't great for wheat anyway.

## Wheat (winter wheat, 7 mu)

I'll plant around **October 10-12**, after the maize is cleared and I've done shallow rotary tillage. I use Jimai 22 (济麦22) — I buy fresh seed every 2-3 years from the seed shop in town, this year I'm using some I kept from last harvest since the crop looked clean. About 15 kg seed per mu, that's what I've always done. A bit heavy maybe but I'd rather have a thick stand.

Fertilizer — before planting I broadcast about **40 kg of compound fertilizer (15-15-15)** per mu and work it in. Then at jointing in late February or early March, I topdress **15 kg of urea** per mu. That comes out to around **17-18 kg of N per mu** total. The extension station guy once told me 14 kg is enough but I've always done a bit more and the wheat looks better for it. Can't afford a bad year.

Irrigation: I'll do **3 times** typically — once before winter if it's dry going into December, once at jointing (most important), and once at grain filling. Sometimes 4 if May is dry. The well is close but diesel isn't cheap, maybe 30 yuan per mu each time.

Weeds I spray once in spring with a herbicide mix. Aphids and powdery mildew sometimes — I watch for them at heading and spray if I see them. No sense spraying if nothing's there.

Expected yield: around **430 kg/mu**. Last year I got 450, year before 410 (dry spring). I plan for 430 and hope for more.

## Maize (summer maize, 7 mu, after wheat)

The moment the combine is done on the wheat around **June 10-12**, I'm out there planting maize with the no-till seeder I share with my neighbor. We've got to get it in by June 15 at the latest. I use **Zhengdan 958 hybrid** — everyone uses it, you can't save hybrid seed so I buy fresh every year, about 4 kg per mu.

Fertilizer is simpler with maize. I put down about **30 kg of compound (15-15-15)** at planting through the seeder, then one topdress of **15 kg urea** at the big trumpet stage (大喇叭口期) in late July. That's roughly **15 kg N/mu** — I go lighter than wheat because the previous wheat crop leaves residue and maize is a shorter season.

Irrigation maybe **1-2 times** — right after planting if no rain, and once in August at tasseling if it's dry. Most years we get enough rain in July.

Pesticide: herbicide once after planting for annual grasses. Corn borer I watch for but don't always spray.

Expected yield: **470-480 kg/mu**. Maize has been good these last few years.

## Cotton (3.1 mu)

This is the headache crop. I plant **late April, around the 25th** when the soil is warm enough. Use a regional variety from the seed shop, about 2 kg per mu with plastic film mulching. I still put down plastic even though it's more work — warms the soil and keeps weeds down.

Fertilizer: **25 kg compound at planting** plus **10 kg urea** at flowering in July. About **12 kg N/mu** total. Cotton doesn't want as much N as wheat — too much N and you get leaves, not bolls.

Irrigation: **2 times**, once at bud formation and once at boll filling if dry.

Pesticide is the biggest cost on cotton. Bollworm, aphids, spider mites — I spray **maybe 5-6 times** through the season. Can't avoid it. Herbicide once too.

Picking is all by hand, starts in **mid-September**, goes through October. First pick is the best quality. My kids come back for 2-3 weekends, my wife and I do the rest. I hire help for maybe 3-4 days at peak, about 120 yuan per day per person.

Expected yield: **250 kg/mu seed cotton** (around 85-90 kg lint). Prices have been unpredictable. If cotton prices stay weak another year or two, I may drop it and put everything in wheat-maize.

## My reasoning in short

I'm not trying to maximize anything. At 65 I want steady, predictable harvests. I fertilize a bit heavier than the extension rates because a yield loss hurts more than wasted urea. I irrigate when I need to and not more — diesel costs real money. I keep cotton out of habit and because the family comes to pick, but I know it may not survive another bad price year. The wheat-maize system is my anchor.
